@U.Windl: The x86-64 System V ABI has a red zone, 128 bytes below RSP which are guaranteed not to be asynchronously clobbered, e.g. by signal handlers. (Kernel code uses -mno-red-zone because interrupts are handled on the same kernel stacks that are in use while kernel code is running. In that case you'd simply use subq $96, %rsp before the mov stores, like you'd do in 32-bit code, or for the Windows x64 ABI, if you wanted to avoid push. Only downside is that -128 fits in disp8 but +128 needs a disp32. For the same reason, you can use add $-128, %rsp vs. sub $128)

If the claim is that mov r, offs(%rsp) is faster than a push, you should include the change of the stack pointer, too. Adding a value once after a block of moves is some way of cheating, because the compiler knows how many pushes were made. Also it seems the "move code" has problems with race conditions (like ISRs that may opush values, also).
